messages:
pagerduty-bot: Incident page fired: service=inference-gateway cluster=prod region=us-west1 trigger=HTTP_5xx_rate threshold=2.5%
alex: acked, oncall here. looking at dashboards now :eyes:
maria: I see a sharp jump in 502/504s starting ~5m ago, spike to ~7% error rate for gateway frontends
devon: linking logs: https://logs.redwood.example.com/gateway?from=1712349600 to=now — lots of timeouts to model-backend-pool
jamal: @alex @maria customer impact: one enterprise customer reported 10% of requests failing, CS is flagged
cs-rep: I'm collecting exact customer ids and will DM sec details (impact severity: high for them)
alex: ok first priorities: isolate whether backend pool or LB. who can run quick tail of gateway pods?
maria: running `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=inference-gateway --since=10m | grep "502" | head -n 50` — hit rate shows connection reset by peer to backend nodes
devon: backend node logs show rapid connection resets and `OOMKill` for several pods around the same time. looks like model-worker prod-4 is flapping
jamal: that's probably cascading. Any autoscaler events?
triage-bot: autoscaler event: replica_set/model-worker scaled from 12 -> 9 at 1712349450, reason: CPU surge then eviction
alex: hmm autoscaler scaled down during busy period due to odd cpu metric. might be bad QoS on those workers causing evictions
maria: mitigation plan: 1) prevent further auto-scaling down 2) add temporary capacity 3) route traffic to dedicated pool as fallback
devon: i'll temporarily disable scale-down: `kubectl patch hpa model-worker -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":12}}'`
alex: do it and confirm when done
devon: done. patched minReplicas to 12 — triage-bot logs: patch applied
jamal: I'll spin up 4 extra model-worker replicas now to soak traffic: `kubectl scale deployment model-worker --replicas=16 -n prod`
maria: also enabling routing fallback: update policy to prefer dedicated-pool for requests > 1s latency. `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routing/policy -d '{"selector":"/llm/generate","fallback":"dedicated-pool"}'`
alex: hold on on the policy push — need canary. We can flip routing for 10% of traffic first. devon, can you apply header-based rollout?
devon: applying header-based rollout: set `X-Fallback-Test: canary` for 10% in the load balancer rule — pushed
maria: after canary, error rate drops from 7% -> 2.1% on canary slice :thumbsup:
jamal: great. I'm scaling model-worker more and checking for OOM reasons — investigating memory config and large batch tasks that may spike mem
alex: also running quick config: bump max_open_files on gateway hosts and increase keepalive timeout from 30s -> 60s to reduce resets: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60` on nodes
triage-bot: deploy-bot: deployment/model-worker scaled to 16 replicas by jamal at 1712350100
maria: monitoring: overall 5xx rate back down to 1.9% across regions. enterprise customer's failure rate dropped to ~0.5% after fallback routing
cs-rep: filing incident ticket to affected customer and offering mitigation steps, will log status update in customer portal in 15m
alex: next steps: - keep minReplicas locked for 2 hours - run root cause: why autoscaler triggered (metrics, misconfigured resource requests) - postmortem owner: jamal
jamal: will own RCA. early hypothesis: model-worker resource requests too low and heavy single-request memory spikes causing evictions during compaction jobs
devon: I'll gather kube events and OOM kill traces and attach to the ticket: `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' -n prod`
maria: adding alert rule tweak: suppress cascade-pager for 10m if autoscaler triggered within last 5m so we don't double-page during scale events (we'll review after RCA)
alex: good. I'm handing off to jamal for RCA. leaving oncall in 20m — devon please be standby in case we see second wave
jamal: acknowledged, will start RCA now. will ping back with timeline and follow-up actions
triage-bot: pagerduty-bot: incident acknowledged by alex at 1712349999
pagerduty-bot: Pager escalations suppressed for 10m while mitigation in progress
cs-rep: quick note: customer SLA breach window started, CS team preparing credit calc and exec summary
alex: thanks everyone. keep updates concise here — if you need immediate hands, call the oncall line. :phone:
jamal: update in 30m or sooner if status changes
